summary: html-to-gutenberg ships heavily obfuscated api.js and monkey-patches a dependency at install time
details: The published tarball includes api.js, a heavily obfuscated file using a hex/XOR string table, string-array rotation, and a Function()-constructor loader wired to the global require. api.js is only referenced from scripts.build (node api.js && tsc), a developer-run build step; it is not reached by scripts.postinstall or by the package main (index.js), so it does not execute on npm install or on require('html-to-gutenberg'). The scripts.postinstall step renames node_modules/fetch-page-assets/index.ts to.bak and copies vendor/fetch-page-assets/index.js over node_modules/fetch-page-assets/index.js; the replacement file is a local HTTP asset fetcher writing to caller-supplied paths with no network callbacks, no secret reads, and no remote fetch at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
